chapter: Brass band and the Lyric Theater
title: Excelsior Brass Band personnel and snare and cymbal setup
summary: Members of the Excelsior band under Na-Na Moret, its size, and how he played snare drum with a cymbal on the side while another man played bass drum.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Were you playing dance band work at the same time?
What? Yeah.
What dance band were you playing with when you played with the Excelsior?
I played at the May Philippe Orchestra. Who was the leader of that? Can you tell us about that? Octave Gasper. He was the leader. He was a bass player.
Before we get away from the Excelsior, who was in that band? We ought to get that.
Well, I'm telling you the fact that it would be hard for me to remember all those fellas. He was the leader. Who was the leader? Uh-huh. Na-Na Moret. He was a trumpet player.
Yes. You called him Na-Na?
We called him Na-Na. I don't know. I don't know which his voice. They called him Na-Na Moret.
Why did you call him that? That's a funny nickname.

Well, that's all we had knew. I knew him, boy. He was an old man. He was strict. Very strict. And he was the leader of the band. I knew that. Remember any other trumpets? I don't know. I couldn't remember. Any of the trombone players? Yeah, I know. Buddy Johnson was one of the trombones. Buddy Johnson was one of the trombones. I believe Peter Bocasch. They played trumpet. Yeah. Peter Bocasch. Hippolyte Shawls. Oh, yeah. I remember them. And old man Giles. You know what I'm talking about? Giles. Albert Giles. He was Albert Giles' daddy. He was playing bass drum.
Is that Clay Giles? The man they call Clay?

That's Albert Giles' daddy. I believe it's Albert Giles Sr. That's right. That's his daddy. Clay was his uncle. You're right. Yeah, because he's a junior. Yeah. Did they have alto horns or saxes? Oh, yeah. What did they use? Yeah. Alto horn. And baritone horn did they have? Yeah, baritone horn. I couldn't remember just who. How many pieces were in the band there, Albert? Huh?
About how many pieces?
Well, it was about a 12 piece. 12 to 15 pieces.
And you played the snare?
Snare drum, yeah. I played snare drum and cymbal.
Oh, yeah. How'd that work?
Well, it worked pretty good.
I mean, not at the same time.
You see, the snare drum. Mm-hmm. And when we'd be going out, I'd play the cymbal.
Oh, I see, yeah. On the bass drum?
No, I wouldn't play the bass drum. I had one ordinary man playing the bass. That was Mr. Jives.
How cool.
He was playing the bass drum. And I was playing just the snare drum and cymbal.
Where'd you hook the cymbal on?
Right on the side of the snare drum.
Right.
Yeah. See, how'd you be going now? Where are your fans? Where did you get that idea from, huh? Well, that was all...
